title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes Sense from Interpret on the chain?
options: Sense is automated; Interpret requires a human
Sense is collection — getting signal somewhere it can be read at all; Interpret is making meaning of it
Sense is quantitative; Interpret is qualitative
Sense happens before a decision; Interpret happens after
questions.explanation: Pulling unanswered intranet searches into one place is Sense. Turning four hundred of them into a ranked list of what the workforce can't find is Interpret. The distinction matters because they fail differently: Sense fails as silence mistaken for consent; Interpret fails as a confident story about a signal that isn't there.

questions.prompt: Why does the chain having a *direction* matter?
options: Because work should always be done in order
Because it shows which links can be automated first
Because errors flow downstream and get more expensive as they go — a bad Sense produces a confident wrong Interpret, a Decide about a problem you don't have, and beautiful Produce nobody needed
Because measurement is only possible at the end of the chain
questions.explanation: And the practical consequence is that speed at Produce can't recover an error made upstream. It arrives faster.

questions.prompt: Which two links has AI transformed while the profession has barely worked them?
options: Produce and Distribute
Decide and Verify
Sense and Interpret
Distribute and Verify
questions.explanation: The function has always held the highest-fidelity record of what employees don't understand (search logs, tickets, open text) and could never read it at volume. That capability now exists and is largely unclaimed. Produce collapsed and is heavily worked; Decide is untouched by AI entirely.

questions.prompt: Practitioners using AI report the highest impact in content strategy (49%), planning (48%), and channel strategy (41%) `[V]`. Why is that finding pointed?
options: Because those percentages are higher than for drafting
Because those are Decide and Interpret work — so practitioners report the most impact in the links they invest in least, while the dominant use remains drafting
Because it shows AI is more useful for strategy than for writing
Because it contradicts the maturity findings from Module 1
questions.explanation: It corroborates Module 1's maturity split from a different direction. Note the limitation: self-reported impact, vendor-commissioned, n=448 North American IC professionals, December 2025: what practitioners believe about their own experience, not a measured outcome.

questions.prompt: What does "being excellent at Produce was a career; it is now a feature" claim, precisely?
options: That production skill no longer has value
That AI produces better work than skilled communicators
That excellence at Produce no longer differentiates, because the floor rose to meet it — not that the skill is worthless
That production work should be outsourced entirely
questions.explanation: Judgment about what makes a sentence land is exactly what makes someone good at reviewing a model's output and at knowing when a message must be human. The claim is about differentiation, not worth.

questions.prompt: Why is Verify described as *newly* expensive?
options: Because verification tools are costly to license
Because when a human wrote the draft, the drafter's own knowledge was a check — and when a model writes it, that check is gone and has to be reinstated deliberately
Because regulations now require verification of internal communications
Because AI output contains more factual errors than human output
questions.explanation: The check was never a formal step; it was a side effect of the writer knowing the subject. Remove the writer and you remove the check, without anyone noticing it was there.

questions.prompt: A communicator spends an hour choosing which four of eleven items make the weekly digest and telling seven sponsors no. Which link is that?
options: Produce, because the output is the digest
Distribute, because it determines what reaches the audience
Decide — choosing what gets said, to whom, and whether at all
Interpret, because it requires judgment about relevance
questions.explanation: And this is the most common misfiling in the function: Decide work logged as Produce because it happened while a document was open. Naming it is the first step to being resourced for it.

questions.prompt: What is the sharpest argument *against* this module's chain framing?
options: That six links is too many to be useful in practice
That if AI had genuinely collapsed Produce, quality would have converged across organizations — and it hasn't, suggesting the floor rose while the ceiling stayed exactly where it was
That Sense and Interpret belong to People Analytics rather than communications
That the chain describes agency work rather than in-house work
questions.explanation: It is the hardest version of the counter and the module says so. If the ceiling is unchanged, then craft at Produce still differentiates, and a framing that calls it a commodity is a status argument dressed as an analysis.
